source_refs.note: Exercise 13.1, Question 10 (book page 248, PDF 253); answer key PDF 310-311. Key's 10(b) 13/3 km/h is wrong; correct 13 km/h.

blocks.prompt: 10 (a) The position of a car after \(t\) hours is given by: \(s(t) = 2t^3 - 3t^2 + t\) (in kilometers). Find the average velocity over the interval \([1, 4]\).
blocks.explanation:
Average velocity = change in position divided by change in time.
Plan: find \(s(4)\) and \(s(1)\), then \(\frac{s(4) - s(1)}{4 - 1}\). No limit is needed here.
steps:
Given: \(s(t) = 2t^3 - 3t^2 + t\) km, interval \(t = 1\) to \(t = 4\) hours.
To find: the average velocity.
Method: \(v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{s(t_2) - s(t_1)}{t_2 - t_1}\) (Section 13.2.1), the slope of the secant line.

Positions at the two ends
\[s(4) = 2(64) - 3(16) + 4 = 128 - 48 + 4 = 84\]
\[s(1) = 2 - 3 + 1 = 0\]
Why: Substitute \(t = 4\) and \(t = 1\) into \(s(t)\).

Average velocity
\[v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{s(4) - s(1)}{4 - 1}\]
\[= \dfrac{84 - 0}{3} = 28\]
Why: Change in position over change in time; km per hour.

Check
\[28 \times 3 = 84 \;\checkmark\]
Why: At \(28\) km/h for \(3\) hours the car covers the \(84\) km change.

blocks.prompt: 10 (b) The position of a car after \(t\) hours is given by: \(s(t) = 2t^3 - 3t^2 + t\) (in kilometers). Find the instantaneous velocity at \(t = 2\).
blocks.explanation:
Instantaneous velocity is the derivative \(s'(2)\).
Plan: first principles at \(t = 2\): \(s(2 + \delta t) - s(2)\), divide by \(\delta t\), take the limit.
steps:
Given: \(s(t) = 2t^3 - 3t^2 + t\), \(t_1 = 2\).
To find: \(v(2) = s'(2)\).
Method: instantaneous velocity at \(t = t_1\) is the derivative \(v(t_1) = \lim_{\delta t \to 0} \frac{s(t_1 + \delta t) - s(t_1)}{\delta t}\) (Section 13.2.1), found here by first principles.

Find \(s(2)\) and \(s(2 + \delta t)\)
\[s(2) = 16 - 12 + 2 = 6\]
\[s(2 + \delta t) = 2(2 + \delta t)^3 - 3(2 + \delta t)^2 + (2 + \delta t)\]
\[= 16 + 24\,\delta t + 12(\delta t)^2 + 2(\delta t)^3\]
\[\quad - 12 - 12\,\delta t - 3(\delta t)^2 + 2 + \delta t\]
\[= 6 + 13\,\delta t + 9(\delta t)^2 + 2(\delta t)^3\]
Why: \((2 + \delta t)^3 = 8 + 12\,\delta t + 6(\delta t)^2 + (\delta t)^3\) and \((2 + \delta t)^2 = 4 + 4\,\delta t + (\delta t)^2\).

Subtract and divide by \(\delta t\)
\[s(2 + \delta t) - s(2) = 13\,\delta t + 9(\delta t)^2 + 2(\delta t)^3\]
\[\dfrac{s(2 + \delta t) - s(2)}{\delta t} = 13 + 9\,\delta t + 2(\delta t)^2\]
Why: The \(6\) cancels; \(\delta t \neq 0\) yet.

Take the limit
\[v(2) = \lim_{\delta t \to 0}\big(13 + 9\,\delta t + 2(\delta t)^2\big)\]
\[= 13\]
Why: Put \(\delta t = 0\).

Check
\[s'(t) = 6t^2 - 6t + 1\]
\[s'(2) = 24 - 12 + 1 = 13 \;\checkmark\]
Why: The general derivative (by the same limit) at \(t = 2\) gives \(13\).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(\frac{13}{3}\) km/h for part (b). This is wrong: \(s'(2) = 6(4) - 6(2) + 1 = 13\), so the instantaneous velocity is \(13\) km/h. (Part (a), \(28\) km/h, is right.)
